raw.assessment: The incumbent provides embedded-caption previews and accessible history. It achieved the timing target in 20/30 sessions, below the required 27/30. H1-O3, O4 and O5 support a hypothesis that completion ordering and weakly retained input associations contribute to unexpected versions; they do not distinguish incorrect render inputs from incorrect preview selection. H1-O7 limits a blanket rendering explanation: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without reported uncertainty. H1-O6 establishes sampled usage, not festival capacity. All evidence is stipulated synthetic data.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each render request to an immutable video-and-caption pair, and show that same pair identity when requesting, browsing and downloading a preview.
openings.delta: Replace reliance on completion numbers and external filename reconstruction with a persistent input association, retaining the last delivered pair and original caption wording.
openings.prediction: Under deliberately reversed completion order, downloaded previews match their selected pair's hashes and editors select their intended pair with fewer corrections.
openings.probe: In private staging, replay overlapping requests using demonstration footage and two caption versions. Verify input/output associations and observe editor selection. Bound implementation to the stipulated effort and retain the existing renderer and delivery format; reject expansion beyond that allowance.
assumptions: Inputs can be retained immutably on existing accounts within four engineer-days and current computing allowance.
Pair labels convey enough meaning for editors to recognize intent.

openings.claim: Do delayed sessions lose most time before the intended pair is ready, or after it is available?
openings.delta: Separate processing delay from identification and inspection delay before choosing the next intervention.
openings.prediction: If history interpretation dominates, delayed sessions show long post-availability intervals and repeated selections; if rendering dominates, most excess time precedes availability. Single-correction sessions provide a limiting comparison.
openings.probe: Align timestamped render events with bounded editor replays recording final edit, intended-pair availability, selection and completed inspection; compare overlapping-request and single-correction cases within one editor-day.
assumptions: Replays approximate real selection behavior; historical render events alone cannot reconstruct attention.

raw.assessment: The stipulated baseline reaches 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions. Mismatched expectations and out-of-order completion are observed, but their causal relationship is unproven. Nine uncomplicated corrections suggest that neither render duration nor version confusion necessarily dominates every session. These are candidate mechanisms; feasibility and the 27/30 target remain unverified.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: make each preview an immutable receipt for an explicitly chosen video hash and caption hash, labeled with a recognizable excerpt of its actual caption wording. Show the editor's selected receipt independently of completion order; downloading resolves only that receipt's paired inputs. Pin the last delivered receipt and its original caption text.
openings.delta: Turns the worksheet's intended pairing into a service-owned object established before rendering, with wording recognizable without decoding sequential preview numbers.
openings.prediction: Deliberately reversing render completion order will no longer change the selected pair; downloaded hashes will match the explicitly confirmed receipt. Selection time should fall if reconstruction is a major delay.
openings.probe: In private staging, use demonstration footage with confusable cuts and captions, then reverse worker completion order and verify receipt, inputs and downloaded artifact together. Use part of the single editor-day to measure identification time; cap implementation within the shared four engineer-days and meter processing.
assumptions: Editors can identify the intended cut when confirming the pair.
The worker can freeze inputs and bind output to the receipt within the budget.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: offer a caption-change audition that plays only changed caption intervals with surrounding motion from the explicitly selected cut, using a private browser overlay and original timestamps. Editors can expand any interval to uninterrupted playback. After approval, request one full embedded-caption preview in the existing format, retaining the delivered version.
openings.delta: Tests whether editing needs continuous full-film rerenders or chiefly rapid inspection of changed words in motion; the final complete preview still establishes delivery wording and timing.
openings.prediction: For repeated text-only edits, audition should reduce full renders and waiting. If continuous context or renderer fidelity dominates, editors will frequently expand intervals or find discrepancies in the final embedded preview.
openings.probe: Spend only the remaining engineering and editor budget on a demonstration prototype, comparing audition judgments with the full embedded render for the same immutable pair. Log context expansions, timing discrepancies, final-preview identification time and processing hours. Evaluate the unchanged 27/30 target in subsequent sessions; do not count audition alone as final-preview success.
assumptions: Existing private accounts can serve paired media to the browser.
Overlay timing can be reconciled with the embedded renderer.
Enough judgments are local to changed intervals to justify the added step.
The prototype fits the shared four engineer-days and 80-hour weekly allowance.

openings.claim: Freeze explicitly selected video/caption hashes into a receipt, recognizable by actual caption wording across request, history and download; selection survives completion reordering. Pin delivered inputs and original wording.
openings.discriminator: Wrong render inputs versus wrong preview selection; receipt integrity alone cannot establish editor intent.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints in design; implementation fit unverified.
openings.probe: Reverse overlapping completions in private staging with confusable demonstration cuts/captions; verify receipt/input/download hashes and editor selection time.
openings.uncertainty: Editors must recognize intended cuts; freezing inputs and useful labels must fit budget.

openings.claim: Separate processing wait from identification and inspection delay.
openings.discriminator: Excess time before intended-pair availability versus repeated selections or long inspection afterward.
openings.probe: Align render events with replays recording final edit, availability, selection and completed inspection; compare overlapping requests with single corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Historical events lack attention data; replays may misrepresent behavior. Nine uncomplicated successes limit blanket explanations.

openings.claim: Audition changed caption intervals with surrounding motion, original timestamps and private browser overlays on the selected cut; allow uninterrupted expansion. After approval, render one complete embedded preview.
openings.discriminator: Local wording judgments reduce rerenders; frequent expansion or final-render discrepancies favor continuous context or renderer fidelity.
openings.fit: Uncertain; preserve delivery format and prior delivered version.
openings.probe: Prototype only within remaining budget; compare audition/full-render judgments, expansions, timing discrepancies, identification time and processing hours.
openings.uncertainty: Private media serving, overlay fidelity, local judgment sufficiency and prototype cost remain unverified.

lineage.reason: With Z1; explicit receipt, wording and stable selection retained.

post_distill.decision: Probe D1/D2 first; D3 conditional on findings and remaining shared four engineer-days/one editor-day. Keep all material on existing private accounts within 80 processing hours/week; sampled 49 hours says nothing about festival demand. Synthetic evidence proves no mechanism. Validate 27/30 new sessions within 15 minutes and zero unintended delivered pairs; audition alone is insufficient.
